clips.send: A son sends this to a dad who skips checkups: the habit Kevin swears by that most people never do, out of quiet anxiety for him.
clips.caption:
Kevin Trudeau brings his car in for a full inspection even when nothing is wrong - brakes, fluids, bearings, tire pressure, every single thing checked before it ever breaks down.

Then he asks the obvious question: why don't we check our bodies the same way?

Most doctors, he says, only run a deeper test - like checking your arteries - once you already have symptoms: chest pain, shortness of breath, numbness. By then you're reacting, not getting ahead of it.

Kevin's own approach: check now, while everything still looks fine, so you actually know where you stand.

When's the last time you got checked before something was wrong?
